audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags "NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere" with 0 sequencing cues. The content layer never gives a number - it says "time dives around your W stacks and his R cooldown" without stating either.
audit.why: Ashen Pursuit is a flat 10 seconds at EVERY rank - it is the only cooldown in his kit that never improves, so the punish window is a constant 10s from level 2 to the end of the game. That is the cleanest "wait for X before you Y" line available in the matchup and it stays true all game, unlike Ritual Nails (10/9/8/7/6) which shrinks under it.
audit.corrected: Flat-10s Ashen Pursuit stated in whys[3], spikes[0].text and mid as the explicit commit trigger.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere notes that Silver Stake scales with the target's MISSING health.
audit.why: His passive on-hit is "increased based on enemy missing Health", so his autos get stronger exactly as the fight goes long and Zac drops. Two consequences the entry never draws: the extended grind Zac normally wants is the trade that most favours Locke, and picking up blobs is not merely sustain - each one restores health and therefore directly reduces the damage of his next auto. It also stacks with Purgatory, so his whole kit points at the same low-HP window.
audit.corrected: Added to whys[0], whys[4], spikes[1].text, wants.you[0] and early.
sources: champ-data/_kits/locke.json (P "additional magic damage On-Hit, increased based on enemy missing Health")

audit.whatIsWrong: Soul Ignition is described only as a "grey-health steroid"; the entry never says when the heal actually lands.
audit.why: The heal is back-loaded: he damages himself for the duration and only "at the end of the duration ... heal(s) back a portion of the damage he takes during the effect". So the payout is deniable. Killing him, or simply breaking the fight off, before Soul Ignition expires means he eats the self-damage and banks nothing - and at 18/17/16/15/14 it is his longest non-ultimate cooldown, so a denied W is a long punish.
sources: champ-data/_kits/locke.json (W "dealing damage to himself. At the end of the duration, Locke will heal back a portion")

audit.whatIsWrong: content spikes[1].text and mid both tell the player to "engage with W stacks ready" / "time dives around your W stacks".
audit.why: Unstable Matter has no stacks. It is a flat 5-second cooldown pulse with no charge or stack mechanic anywhere in the kit. The advice points at a resource that does not exist, so a player cannot act on it even in principle.
audit.corrected: Both lines rewritten to key off things that do exist - his missing-health passive and the flat 10s Ashen Pursuit.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zac.json (W cooldown "5", no stack mechanic in description or flags)

audit.whatIsWrong: content early calls it "his Q Ritual Nails on-hit poke".
audit.why: Conflates two abilities. Ritual Nails is a thrown 950-range projectile that damages and MARKS; the on-hit damage is Silver Stake, the passive. The marks are then consumed by his attacks for bonus damage. Calling Q an on-hit hides the two-step (mark, then cash) that the whole trade pattern turns on.
audit.corrected: early now separates the mark from the on-hit that cashes it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/locke.json (Q "marking enemies hit. Locke can consume the marks to deal bonus damage with his attacks"; P Silver Stake on-hit)

audit.whatIsWrong: content late leans on "revive through the execute he saved all game" without noting Cell Division's cooldown.
audit.why: Cell Division is a 5-minute cooldown. Once it has fired, Zac has no revive for a very long stretch - longer than most objective cycles - so a second dive inside that window is played without the safety net the line implicitly promises. Against a champion whose ultimate is an execute, knowing whether the passive is up is the whole decision.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zac.json (P "This ability has a 5 minute cooldown")

audit.why: Win rate 48.57% over 593 games - the largest sample in this slice. The chart (Skill/Skill/Skill/Zac/Skill/Zac/Zac) leans Zac, which sits oddly against a sub-50% win rate, but the entry is explicitly written as a favoured lane that Zac loses on the map rather than in it, and the full layer says so. Left alone rather than flipped on one number.
